Summary subgroup statistics

Source: R/group_data_summary.R
group_data_summary.Rd

Convert published subgroup statistics into the standardized format used by retrogroup.

Usage

group_data_summary(
  data,
  variable,
  level,
  patients,
  log_hazard_ratio,
  standard_error = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with one row per subgroup level. Must have the columns named by the other arguments. Other columns are ignored.

variable

Character string, name of the column in data with the name of the subgroup variable. The column must be character with non-empty, non-missing values.

level

Character string, name of the column in data with the level of the subgroup variable. The column must be character or factor with non-empty, non-missing values.

patients

Character string, name of the column in data with the number of patients to assign to each level of the reconstructed subgroup variable, usually taken from the publication. See the details section for when these counts may differ from the publication. The column must contain strictly positive whole numbers with no missing values.

log_hazard_ratio

Character string, name of the column in data with the published log hazard ratio of treatment versus control in each subgroup level. The column must be numeric and finite with no missing values.

standard_error

Character string or NULL. If a character string, name of the column in data with the published standard error of the log hazard ratio in each subgroup level. The column must be numeric, finite, and strictly positive with no missing values. If NULL, the standard errors are unavailable, and the standard_error column of the output is NA.

Value

A tibble with one row per subgroup level, in the same order as data, and the following columns:

  • variable: character, name of the subgroup variable.

  • level: character, level of the subgroup variable.

  • patients: integer, number of patients in the subgroup level.

  • log_hazard_ratio: numeric, published log hazard ratio of treatment versus control in the subgroup level.

  • standard_error: numeric, published standard error of the log hazard ratio, or NA if standard_error is NULL.

Details

Each row of data is one level of a subgroup variable. A subgroup variable must have at least two levels, the levels must be unique within the subgroup variable, and every level must have a strictly positive number of patients.

The patient counts must have the same total for every subgroup variable, because every subgroup variable partitions the same patients. The counts are the sizes of the levels of the reconstructed subgroup variables, so they need not copy the publication verbatim. Published counts are the natural starting point, but they sometimes do not add up to the total number of patients in the study, for example because of missing subgroup data or typographical errors. In that case, choosing counts that add up to the total number of patients is a decision about the reconstruction, not an attempt to recover the true counts from the clinical study. Please disclose that decision transparently wherever the reconstructed data or downstream results are reported.

See also

Other data: group_data_patient()

Examples

  data <- group_example_summary()
  group_data_summary(
    data,
    variable = "variable",
    level = "level",
    patients = "patients",
    log_hazard_ratio = "log_hazard_ratio",
    standard_error = "standard_error"
  )
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   variable level      patients log_hazard_ratio standard_error
#>   <chr>    <chr>         <int>            <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 age      under 60        280           -0.169          0.178
#> 2 age      60 or over      339           -0.546          0.160
#> 3 node4    no              453           -0.417          0.153
#> 4 node4    yes             166           -0.312          0.190
#> 5 sex      female          312           -0.147          0.162
#> 6 sex      male            307           -0.656          0.179
  group_data_summary(
    data,
    variable = "variable",
    level = "level",
    patients = "patients",
    log_hazard_ratio = "log_hazard_ratio"
  )
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   variable level      patients log_hazard_ratio standard_error
#>   <chr>    <chr>         <int>            <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 age      under 60        280           -0.169             NA
#> 2 age      60 or over      339           -0.546             NA
#> 3 node4    no              453           -0.417             NA
#> 4 node4    yes             166           -0.312             NA
#> 5 sex      female          312           -0.147             NA
#> 6 sex      male            307           -0.656             NA
